name: autorestic
description: `upgrade` overwrites own binary + triggers restic self-update, zero checksum/sig.
limitations: AI-generated static source analysis. Confirm the affected version, platform, update channel, and cited control flow before relying on this classification.

later_review_audit.description: autorestic provides a release-based upgrade command for its own executable. The inspected implementation supports that channel identification; the full artifact-authentication policy and the separate restic update dependency remain unresolved.
limitations: New default-branch snapshot rather than the original study release; restic's delegated self-update and release-side integrity controls were not assessed, and no exploitability conclusion is made.

original_evidence.text: | **autorestic** (github.com/cupcakearmy/autorestic) | Y | N (manual `autorestic upgrade` CLI command only; not run automatically at startup) | Y (downloads a `.bz2` archive from the latest GitHub release and overwrites its own binary at `/usr/local/bin`, and also can drive `restic self-update`) | https in practice (URLs come from `api.github.com` and GitHub `browser_download_url`), but code uses plain Go `http.Get` with **no explicit scheme enforcement, no TLS pinning, and no cert-verification hardening** | N (no manifest, no signature file of any kind is fetched — only raw GitHub Releases JSON) | **none** — archive is decompressed and installed with zero checksum or signature check | n/a (no key exists in this flow) | `autorestic/internal/bins/bins.go:34` (`http.Get` for JSON), `:60-116` (`downloadAndInstallAsset` — bzip2 decompress → `os.Rename` straight into install path, no hash check anywhere), `:125` (restic release URL), `:156` (autorestic release URL); CLI wiring: `autorestic/cmd/upgrade.go:8-21` |
